rationale: Evidence: all 60 development trials across oval, s-bend and slalom ended off_track with zero completions. Iteration 1 raised oval progress to 0.20 but left s-bend at 0.04 and slalom at 0.10. Max error sits at about 0.061 m on every track, which is the off-track limit, so the robot leaves the tape by a consistent overshoot rather than slow drift. Line-loss events fell to 0 on oval, so the wider sensor spread and 16 mm sensors are working. Steering oscillation rose from 0.075 to 0.117 on oval when kd went from 0.1 to 0.5 with kp raised to 4. The likely cause is that kd is acting on a signal that changes very quickly, because a sensor crossing takes about 0.03 s at about 1 m/s. That makes kd*(d signal/dt) large and noisy, so it adds chatter instead of damping. Changes: (1) kd 0.5 to 0.2 to cut derivative jitter; (2) kp 4.0 to 3.0 to reduce overshoot per unit of offset; (3) base_speed 1.4 to 1.2 because survival matters more than speed while no run finishes, since a completion is worth 500 points; (4) sensor y moved from 0.03 to 0.05 m ahead of the axle so the sensors see the line earlier, which reduces the lag that produces overshoot at a given speed. Geometry x-spread, sensor size, wheel_track and mass are kept so the effect of the controller changes can be read cleanly. Expected result: max_error below 0.05 on s-bend and slalom, steering_oscillation back near 0.07 or lower, and progress above 0.3 on all tracks. Hypotheses to check next: (H1) if s-bend still stops at about 0.04 progress, the first bend is too tight for this speed and base_speed should drop to about 1.0; (H2) if oscillation is still high, the sensor noise is driving kd and kd should go to 0; (H3) if the robot survives but does not finish, base_speed must rise, since finishing needs about 1.5 m/s average. Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and noise_robustness per track.
